newsitem.title: USA: Boeing rejects Airbus sales claim.
newsitem.headline: Boeing rejects Airbus sales claim.

text.p: Boeing Co Tuesday rejected an Airbus Industrie executive's claim that the European airplane maker was outselling Boeing in North America this year.

"Boeing has enjoyed an excellent year in terms of orders, reflecting the superior value of Boeing airplanes and services," Boeing said in a brief statement. "Of the 621 Boeing airplanes ordered through November 1996, 458 of them are from U.S. customers. By comparison, based on announced orders this year, Airbus has booked 291 orders, of which 147 are identified as U.S. customers."
Earlier, Jonathan Schofield, Airbus chief for North America said Airbus was outperforming Boeing.
"It's an arrogant statement but I believe we're outselling Boeing this year in North America," said Schofield, chairman and chief executive of Airbus Industrie of North America.
He told a meeting in Brussels of the European Aviation Club on air travel deregulation that Airbus was not facing too many structural problems in North America.
"No one has given us a barrier to entry," he said.
"I feel quite well accepted and as long as we're selling at the rate we're selling at in North America, I consider the company extremely successful," he said.
Boeing said it has also been successful overseas.
"European customers have ordered 64 Boeing airplanes this year as compared to 19 for Airbus," the Seattle-based aircraft maker said. "These are the facts, not hype."
